notes: masssave.com returns a Cloudflare bot challenge to automated fetches, so Mass Save amounts were verified from MassCEC's Clean Energy Lives Here pages (MassCEC + DOER, state agencies that republish Mass Save offers) and mass.gov. Re-check masssave.com by hand before quoting per-ton or partial-home amounts.

facts.program: Mass Save air-source heat pump rebate (standard)
facts.claim: Up to $8,500 for a whole-home air-source heat pump system
facts.eligibility: Mass Save electric customers (Eversource, National Grid, Unitil, Cape Light Compact). Not MLP towns.
facts.notes: Partial-home amounts: see 'Mass Save ASHP rebate table 2026' below.

facts.claim: Whole-home heat pump may be no cost or up to $16,000 if household qualifies for Enhanced Rebates
facts.eligibility: Income-qualified households only (moderate-income and income-eligible tiers). NOT the standard amount.
facts.notes: Site previously showed $16,000 as if everyone gets it. Correct framing: $8,500 standard; up to $16,000 or no cost only for income-qualified.

facts.claim: Enhanced offers for households at 61-80% AMI; 100% of eligible electrification cost for households below 80% AMI (income-eligible)
facts.notes: Use as general framing only; exact income cutoffs change yearly - send readers to masssave.com income-eligible page.

facts.claim: 0% interest loan
facts.eligibility: Mass Save customers; eligible measures (heat pumps, insulation, HPWH, battery if enrolled in ConnectedSolutions)

facts.claim: Low-interest loan for income-qualified households
facts.amount: up to $100,000 at up to 2% interest, up to 20 years

facts.claim: Free (no-cost) home energy assessment; unlocks weatherization incentives
facts.notes: Online assessments also listed by DOER: https://www.mass.gov/energy-programs-for-individuals

facts.claim: 75%-100% off insulation, air sealing and weather stripping
facts.eligibility: 100% generally for income-qualified households or certain 1-4 unit buildings; 75% standard
facts.notes: Also $75/window for replacing single-pane with triple-pane windows.

facts.program: Mass Save heat pump water heater
facts.claim: Instant rebate when replacing an existing electric, oil, propane or gas water heater
facts.notes: MassCEC example: $3,200 installed, $2,450 after rebate. Rebate never exceeds cost.

facts.claim: Rebate on induction cooktop when switching from gas or propane
ENERGY STAR clothes dryer rebate
facts.notes: Appliance rebates are small; none exceed product cost.

facts.claim: One-time payment for installing air-source heat pumps
facts.amount: about $250-$1,000 for a 2,000 sq ft whole-home system

facts.claim: Primary solar incentive for National Grid, Eversource and Unitil customers; pays per kWh over time
facts.amount: MassCEC example: about $300/yr for an 8 kW system

facts.claim: 15% of solar system cost
Pay for letting utility use battery during peak events
facts.amount: 5 kW continuous battery earns about $1,375/yr in summer events

facts.claim: 41 MLPs serve all or part of 50 municipalities; these towns are not in Mass Save electric programs and use their MLP's own rebates
facts.eligibility: Towns incl. Belmont, Braintree, Chicopee, Concord, Danvers, Hingham, Holyoke, Hudson, Ipswich, Mansfield, Marblehead, Norwood, Peabody, Reading, Shrewsbury, Taunton, Wakefield, Wellesley, Westfield and others
facts.notes: Mass Save gas-side offers may still apply where the gas utility is a Mass Save sponsor. DOER MLP Z-Loan offers zero-interest loans to MLP customers: https://www.mass.gov/energy-programs-for-individuals

facts.claim: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (25C) and Residential Clean Energy Credit (25D) ended for property placed in service after December 31, 2025
facts.notes: Terminated by Public Law 119-21 (July 2025). Mass Save's own pages also say IRA credits expired end of 2025.

facts.claim: Whole-home $2,650/ton up to $8,500; Partial-home $1,125/ton up to $8,500; Basic $250/ton up to $2,500; income-based enhanced up to $16,000 or no cost via Turnkey
facts.eligibility: Replacing oil, propane or electric resistance (electric sponsor) or natural gas (gas sponsor: Berkshire Gas, Eversource, Liberty, National Grid, Unitil). Installed Jan 1-Dec 31 2026 by a Heat Pump Installer Network contractor; ENERGY STAR Cold Climate; whole-home needs sufficient weatherization + verification form. Partial-home: $500 weatherization bonus + $500 sizing bonus; integrated controls required.
facts.notes: Mass Save cost example: $22,000 install -> $13,500 net standard, $6,000 net enhanced. Gas-heated homes in MLP towns may qualify via their Mass Save gas sponsor. Live masssave.com blocks bots; read via Wayback snapshot July 16, 2026.

facts.claim: Whole-home $13,500; partial-home $2,000/ton up to $13,500; income-based enhanced up to $25,000

facts.program: DPU order on 2025-2027 Mass Save plan
facts.claim: DPU cut the three-year budget by $500 million (to about $4.5B); residential budgets down about 25% gas and 15% electric
facts.notes: Pages must not claim the cut directly caused the $10,000 -> $8,500 change; say both happened.

facts.claim: $50 ENERGY STAR clothes dryer rebate (MassCEC lists it for heat pump dryers); $500 induction cooktop rebate when switching from gas or propane
facts.notes: Washer and fridge-recycling amounts NOT verified; pages now say 'check current amount'. Old pages claimed a $200 heat pump dryer rebate and a $75 recycling payment.

facts.claim: Systems <=25 kW AC get a flat incentive per kWh generated
facts.notes: Payment term not confirmed on this page; pages now say 'fixed term' instead of '10 to 20 years'.

facts.claim: 0% loan for MLP customers for measures recommended in a home energy assessment
facts.eligibility: MLP electric customers heating with MLP electricity, municipal gas, or delivered fuel; not eligible for Mass Save. Excludes solar and EV chargers.
facts.notes: Apply at myz-loan.com. Assessment via ENE or NextZero.

facts.claim: Efficiency program for about 28 participating MLPs
facts.notes: The '$100/kWh battery rebate' claim could not be verified; removed.

facts.claim: No verified upfront Mass Save per-kWh battery rebate; earnings come from ConnectedSolutions (see above) and the SMART storage adder
facts.notes: Pages claimed a '$100/kWh capacity rebate' and '$225/kW' / '$200/kW' rates; replaced with MassCEC's $1,375/yr for 5 kW example.

facts.claim: 0% loan up to $25,000 for rooftop solar, fully forgiven after 20 years of owner-occupancy
facts.eligibility: Boston 1-4 family owner-occupants, income <=135% AMI, <$100,000 in assets; about 20 households

facts.claim: National Grid (Massachusetts Electric) serves Lynn, Salem, Brockton, Worcester, Lowell, Quincy, Fall River, Lawrence. Not in National Grid's list (Eversource): Boston, Cambridge, Somerville, Newton, Springfield, New Bedford.
facts.notes: Lynn, Lowell and Quincy pages wrongly said Eversource; fixed. Eversource-specific EV charger ($1,500/Managed Charging) and rate numbers removed from those pages. Per-kWh rate figures removed from all MA heat pump pages (unverified).

facts.claim: As of Jan 1, 2026, heat pumps with refrigerant GWP over 700 (incl. R-410A) removed from the Heat Pump Qualified Product List
facts.notes: 'R-32 or R-454B only' on pages is a fair simplification.

facts.claim: No-cost virtual or in-person assessment, plus no-cost Online Energy Assessment; 866-527-7283. Income-qualified: insulation, air sealing, heat pumps up to no cost.
